sentences.text: Coccosteus was a small placoderm, a type of armored fish, with the species C. cuspidatus measuring between 29.6 and 39.4 cm in length.
This animal possessed a joint between the armor of its body and skull, a trait shared with other arthrodires.
Coccosteus kept its beak sharp by having the edges of its dental plates grind against each other.
Coccosteus looked similar to the giant Dunkleosteus, but its eyes were positioned closer to the end of its snout.
The largest Coccosteus specimens measured about 40 cm, while the average length was between 20 and 24 cm.
C. cuspidatus serves as an important index fossil in the Devonian sequence of northern Scotland's Orcadian Basin.
Up to 49 species have been identified since the genus was described, many later reclassified.
The genus Coccosteus was described by Agassiz in 1843.
The genus Coccosteus was originally described by Agassiz in 1841.
Its longer jaws and wide-opening mouth allowed the animal to consume fairly large prey.
The up-and-down movement of Coccosteus's skull allowed more water to be pumped through its gills.
Researchers suggest Coccosteus may have supplemented its diet by filtering organic material from mud using its gills.
Coccosteus is the type genus for the family Coccosteidae, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
Fossils of Coccosteus have been found throughout Europe and North America.
Most Coccosteus fossils are found in freshwater sediments, suggesting the animal may have occasionally entered saltwater.
Coccosteus lived during the Middle to Late Devonian periods.
Coccosteus lived from the Emsian to the Famennian stages, between 410.62 and 358.86 million years ago.
